hypothesis: If eggs are never oblate, then in a broad sample of bird eggs essentially every egg (to measurement error) has maximum breadth no greater than its length, i.e. elongation (length/breadth) is at least 1.
pass_criterion: Using individual egg length and breadth (DATAraweggs.csv), the fraction of eggs with length/breadth < 0.95 (clearly oblate, beyond a 5% allowance for caliper error and rounding) is ≤ 0.1%, AND no species with n ≥ 5 eggs has a mean length/breadth below 0.98.
fail_criterion: More than 1% of eggs have length/breadth < 0.95, or at least one species with n ≥ 5 eggs has a mean length/breadth < 0.95. Either result means oblate eggs occur as a regular, non-error phenomenon and the claim is refuted. Results between these thresholds are reported as inconclusive.
interpretation: Thompson's 'prolate spheroid' is a solid of revolution whose axis (length) exceeds its equatorial diameter (breadth); 'oblate' means the axis is shorter than the equatorial diameter. 'Egg' means the hard-shelled bird egg, the scope of the chapter. Modern reinterpretation: real eggs are not exact solids of revolution (many are asymmetric or pyriform), so the test checks only the prolate-vs-oblate distinction via the length/breadth ratio, taking maximum breadth as the equatorial diameter. Tolerances are needed because ratios near 1 (spherical eggs, e.g. owls) are neither clearly prolate nor oblate, and measurements carry error. Column names must be confirmed from the dataset's README.txt before analysis; I have not seen them.

dataset.name: The evolution of egg shape in birds: Evolutionary constraints and adaptations
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data by Montgomerie, Birkhead, Thompson and Hemmings)
dataset.why_it_fits: The Dryad record lists DATAraweggs.csv (raw egg measurements) and DATAeggshape.csv (egg shape data) covering eggs of 955 bird species per the associated paper's abstract. The raw file should supply per-egg length and breadth for the length/breadth test. I confirmed the file names on the landing page but not the column names; README.txt in the record documents the fields and should be read first.
